questions.q: In Apex, how is a SOSL search term written, as opposed to in the Query Editor or API?
options: As a bind variable, e.g. FIND :searchTerm
In curly braces, e.g. FIND {Acme}, exactly the same as the Query Editor
In double quotes only
In single quotes, e.g. FIND 'Acme'
questions.explain: The Query Editor and API use curly braces around the search term; Apex uses single quotes for the same FIND statement.

questions.q: What does the * wildcard match in a SOSL search term?
options: Exactly one character
Zero or more characters
Only whitespace
Nothing — SOSL has no wildcards
questions.explain: * matches zero or more characters in a SOSL search term, the same meaning as % in SOQL's LIKE.

questions.q: If you omit the IN SearchGroup clause entirely, what scope does SOSL default to?
options: SIDEBAR FIELDS
NAME FIELDS
ALL FIELDS
No search is performed without this clause
questions.explain: ALL FIELDS is the default search scope when IN SearchGroup is omitted.

questions.q: A search scoped to IN PHONE FIELDS would fail to find a match for a term that only appears in a Name field. Why?
options: Narrowing the search group changes which fields are actually searched — PHONE FIELDS doesn't include name-type fields
PHONE FIELDS searches every field type, so this scenario couldn't happen
SOSL automatically expands PHONE FIELDS to include NAME FIELDS
Phone fields and name fields are always identical in Salesforce
questions.explain: The SearchGroup clause genuinely restricts which fields are searched, not just how results are ranked — a term outside that scope won't be found.

questions.q: What does a bare FIND {Acme} with no RETURNING clause return?
options: Only the Name field of matching Account records
Every field on every matching record
A compile error, since RETURNING is required
Only the IDs of matching records across every searchable object
questions.explain: Without RETURNING, a SOSL search returns just record IDs across searchable objects — RETURNING is what lets you specify actual fields to get back.
